newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Petrogal near deal to sell stake to Aram.
newsitem.headline: Petrogal near deal to sell stake to Aram.

text.p: Portuguese state oil company Petrogal is close to reaching an agreement to sell a stake to Saudi Aramco, Under-Secretary for Energy Jose Penedos said.

"We are at a conclusive phase in terms of finding a strategic partner," Penedos told reporters at a ceremony marking the opening of an oil pipeline linking the southern port of Sines and Aveiras, 50 km (30 miles) north of Lisbon.
Earlier, Penedos told Diario Economico newspaper "Conditions have been created to reach an outline agreement (with Saudi Aramco) by the end of June."
Saudi Aramco, which has held talks in recent months to buy a stake in Petrogal, has boosted its offer, paving the way for a possible outline agreement by end-June, Lisbon newspapers reported.

Diario Economico said it had learned that Saudi Aramco had raised its offer following a revaluation of Petrogal by J.P.Morgan based on its 1996 accounts, which valued the Portuguese oil company at at least 230 billion escudos.
Newspapers did not give details of the offer.
Penedos did not comment on the negotiations under way with Saudi Aramco.
Oil market sources said Petrocontrol, a group of private shareholders which owns 45 percent of Petrogal, could form a new company with Saudi Aramco.
The new company, in which Petrocontrol and Saudi Aramco would each hold 50 percent, would hold 70 percent of Petrogal's capital of 103 billion escudos.
The Portuguese government would retain 10 percent of Petrogal and the other 20 percent would be floated.
